Subject: MAP: Integration build plan (SDK streaming, tool calling, structured outputs) - draft

Hi Sara —

Great to speak earlier today. As promised, attaching a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the Integration Build Plan milestone. High-level recap below and a few asks to keep momentum:

Quick recap (from discovery)
- Goal: ACME wants productized streaming SDK + tool-calling support and structured JSON outputs for analytics pipelines.
- Key success criteria: <3rd-party tool latency under 250ms per call, structured outputs match ACME schema v1, SDKs supported for primary client platforms.

Attached MAP milestone: Integration build plan (summary)
- Milestone name: Integration build plan
- Deliverables: SDK integration (Python/Node + Java preview), streaming (SSE/chunked streaming + backpressure guidelines), tool calling connectors (outbound HTTP/webhooks + managed connectors), structured outputs (JSON schema + validation tests)
- Owners: ACME: Tom Huang (Eng) — implement integration on product side; Redwood: Rishi Malhotra (SE) — integration support & SDK samples; Redwood CS: Vanessa Ortiz — onboarding/rollout plan
- Dependencies: Legal review for data flows, SSO + firewall egress configuration, availability of ACME dev env for integration testing
- Target milestone completion: 2027-02-28
- Target close date (MAP / commercial): 2027-03-15

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm Tom as the technical owner for the integration work?
2) Do you want us to share a short SDK demo + conformance checklist in the tech working session next week?
3) Are any internal compliance docs (FAQ, data retention) we should get to Legal now?

I attached: MAP_v1_ACME.docx (draft), integration_diagram.png, redwood_sdk_conformance_checklist.pdf

Proposed follow-ups
- Tech working session (30–45m) to walk SDK streaming and function-calling examples: Jan 13 or Jan 14 — please share availability
- We’ll update the MAP after the call and send a version with explicit milestones and acceptance criteria.

Thanks — excited to keep this moving.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap and the draft MAP. A few quick clarifying Qs from our side before we lock owners: 

1) Streaming: Can you confirm whether Redwood uses server-sent events (SSE) or a chunked HTTP stream for streaming? We care about reconnect/ordering semantics.
2) SDKs: We saw Python and Node listed — does Redwood have a Java SDK or a Java roadmap? Our backend services are primarily Java-based.
3) Tool calling: Do you have published examples of the managed connectors (e.g., calling our internal search indices) and how auth is handled?

Tom is CC’d but out until Monday afternoon (PST). If we can get answers today that will help us brief him before the tech session.

Also — legal will likely want a diagram of data flows and a short bullets doc on retention. If you could include both in the next MAP update that would be great.

Thanks —
Sara
Product Manager | ACME Corp
sara.lin@acme.com

Hi Sara — thanks for the quick follow-up and great questions. Answers inline below + updated asks. I’m attaching an updated MAP and the integration diagram with data flows for Legal.

1) Streaming: Redwood supports chunked HTTP streaming and Server-Sent Events (SSE) for browser-native clients. For backend SDKs we recommend chunked streaming with explicit sequence numbers in the payload for ordering and resumable cursors for reconnects. Typical tail-to-first-byte latency is 100–200ms in our hosted region benchmarks; we’ll share p95 numbers for your expected region in the tech session.

2) SDKs: We ship first-class Python and Node SDKs. Java is on our roadmap as a preview package this quarter — we can provide a preview Java client and guidance for integration testing during the tech working session. Rishi will own the technical walkthrough and provide the preview client.

3) Tool calling & auth: We have sample connectors for outbound HTTP/webhooks and can implement a managed connector pattern (token-based service account with scoped permissions). For calling internal search indices we typically recommend a proxy service on the customer side; we’ll include a code snippet in the conformance checklist and example repo link.

What I updated in the MAP (attached)
- Added data-flow diagram for Legal (integration_diagram.png)
- Explicit owners: ACME: Tom Huang (Engineering), Sara Lin (Product); Redwood: Rishi Malhotra (SE) & Vanessa Ortiz (CS)
- Milestone target completion: 2027-02-28 (integration complete, QA passes)
- Acceptance criteria: SDK sample passes conformance checklist; structured outputs match ACME schema v1 (we’ll include test vectors)
- Target commercial close: 2027-03-15

Proposed tech sessions
- Wed Jan 13, 10:00–10:45 PT — SDK + streaming deep-dive (Rishi)
- Thu Jan 14, 9:00–9:45 PT — Tool calling & structured outputs (Vanessa + Rishi)

Please confirm Tom as the tech owner and which of the two slots works for you. We’ll send calendar invites and a short pre-read.

Best,
Marissa Cole
